note: Phase 2 batch 1, 2026-11-23. One entry per block and platform: the judge's verdict and what the challenger found.

defects: escape-cancels (and focus handling): a mouse press does not leave focus on the button, so Escape cannot cancel a mouse-armed confirm. The port puts tabindex="-1" on the label, spinner and notice spans (and the svg); the mousedown lands on the label span, which takes focus (activeElement during mousedown = SPAN[tabindex=-1]; original and svelte = BUTTON), and when that span is swapped out on arming focus drops to BODY (activeElement after arming = BODY; original = BUTTON). Pressing Escape 400ms after a mouse arm: original is back to "Remove", data-active removed, status empty within 180ms; vue is still "Remove signup", data-active=true, status "Press again to remove signup" 180ms and 580ms later (screenshot confirm-button-vue-16-mouse-escape-180ms.png shows the armed red button, original shows the plain Remove key). Keyboard-armed Escape works (Tab, Enter, Escape matches the original).

swap-motion: the entering label is stretched horizontally during the width change instead of keeping its size. Sampled label width while entering: vue "Remove signup" 57.06px -> 84.46px over the first ~75ms (final 93.08) and re-entering "Remove" 79.19px -> 55.88px (final 48.55); the original's labels stay at a constant 91.95px / 48.44px throughout (layout="position"). Button width spring itself matches (70.55 -> 116.4 peak -> 115.08 in ~300ms vs original 70.44 -> 115.25 -> 113.95 in ~280-300ms).

defects: pointer-press-track: a click whose press and release land in the same frame is animated with the spring instead of jumping. Measured with mouse down and up with no hold at 90% of the price track: thumb centre went 60, 60.07, 62.48, 66.64, 71.73, 76.37, 80.9, 84.15, 86.75, 88.58, 89.71, 90.42, 90.77, 90.89 (overshoot 0.89%), settling after about 367ms over 22 frames; the fill width did the same (50 to 80, peak 80.89). The original and the Vue port jump 60 to 90 in one frame (about 17ms) in the same test. With a 40ms or 100ms hold the Svelte port is also instant, so this only shows on very fast clicks (tap to click, scripted clicks). First run confirmed it independently: 300ms after a plain click at the track ends the thumb was still at -0.57% and 100.1% while the original was at 0 and 100. Likely cause in RangeSlider.svelte: motionTo's update calls controls.stop() on the duration-0 animation before it has applied a frame, then starts the spring from the old value when dragging returns to null

defects: repeat-press-loading / focus retention: a mouse click never leaves focus on the button. The inner motion.span carries tabindex="-1" (LoadingButton.vue line ~145, also on the check motion.path), so the click focuses that span, and when the span is swapped out focus drops to BODY. Measured after a real mouse click on Subscribe: document.activeElement = BODY during loading, success and idle (original and Svelte: BUTTON in all three). The sampler shows focus=false on the Vue button in every mouse run (subscribe, pay, apply, hold-press), focus=true in the original.

keyboard-activate: consequence of the above. After clicking Subscribe with the mouse and waiting for idle, pressing Space starts a new cycle in the original (aria-busy at +18ms, Subscribed at +1418ms) and in Svelte, but does nothing in Vue (no state change over 4s). Keyboard activation works in Vue only when focus arrived by Tab.

defects: success-subscribe: the check mark is never drawn with motion enabled. The check path's computed stroke-dasharray stays '0px, 1px' for the whole 2000ms success state (original and Vue go 0 > 1px in about 285ms). Screenshots loading-button-svelte-x-3-success.png and loading-button-svelte-4-subscribe-success.png show only a dot left of 'Subscribed'. Under reduced motion the check is drawn (dasharray '1px, 1px').

success-sticky: same bug on Pay. 'Paid' is shown with a dot instead of a check and it stays that way indefinitely (loading-button-svelte-8-pay-paid.png, loading-button-svelte-12-end.png, taken many seconds after success).

shrink-loading (expand back): the port springs border-radius in px from 999 to 6, so the button stays a full pill for about 400ms after success/error (radius 330px at +150ms, 64px at +283ms, below the 20px clamp only at about +380ms, 6px at +530ms). The original sets the radius immediately: 6px vertical ('15%') from the first frame of the expansion. Visible in loading-button-svelte-x-3-success.png (pill) versus loading-button-orig-x-3-success.png (6px corners) at the same moment. Note the checklist text asks for an animated radius; the original does not do that.

press-scale (release): on release the scale first moves the wrong way, 0.970 > 0.954 (about 50ms after release) before returning to 1; original and Vue return monotonically 0.970 > 1. Same thing on a quick click: a brief 1.003 to 1.004 blip. Small (about 6px on the full-width Pay button) but measured on every release (hold on idle Subscribe, idle Pay and Paid).

defects: keyboard-activate / focus: after a real mouse click on a heart, focus does not stay on the button, so Enter/Space no longer toggles it. Measured on the Lamp button: at mousedown document.activeElement is path{tabindex=-1} (the fill path), after mouseup it is body (focus log: focusin:path{-1}, focusout:path{-1}); Enter then leaves aria-pressed unchanged (enterToggles=false). Same on the unsaved Mug: active element body after click, Space and Enter both leave aria-pressed=false. Original: Enter/Space after a click toggles in both modes (normal: focus on the inner span and aria-pressed false->true->false; reduced motion: focus on the button). Svelte: focus on the button, toggles. Cause: tabindex="-1" added to motion.span and motion.path in FavoriteButton.vue makes them click-focusable inside the button, and the focused path is unmounted on unsave. Happens in normal and reduced-motion contexts.

attribute difference: Vue renders tabindex="-1" on the circle span and on the fill path (innerFocusables ["SPAN:-1","path:-1"]); the original has tabindex="0" on the span in normal motion and no tabindex at all in reduced motion, and never one on the path.

missedDefects: Interrupted fill transition (from source, not shown in data): FavoriteButton.svelte lines 119-134 `fillOut` returns `css: (tt) => `opacity: ${tt}`` from 1 and ignores the current opacity and scale. The original `exit={{ opacity: 0 ... }}` animates from the live value. A click during the ~83-100 ms entry, or a re-click during the 120 ms exit, can jump the heart to full opacity or snap from scale>1 to 1, and may briefly show two fills. The script's rapid test uses 45 ms gaps but only reads the state after 1200 ms, so this would not show up.

Count path rewritten and never executed: lines 136-164 (`countItems`, `countIn`, `countOut`, `popOut`). The judge lists it as untested. Its checklist item count-roll is scope all, so a core feature of the block (the animated count) is unverified for Svelte.

missedDefects: QuantityStepper.vue adds an attribute the original does not have: `<motion.span :key="value" tabindex="-1" ...>` on the rolling digit. The original's `<motion.span key={value} ... className="block">` has no tabindex. The result is an aria-hidden element that is script-focusable. The script's state dump reads tabindex only from the input and buttons, so it never saw this. It is not a Tab stop, so tab-order still passes. This is minor.

Typing the digit already shown (2 over the selected 2) enters draft mode in the port. In `onInput`, `draft.value = el.value.replace(...)` always runs. The original gets no React change event, so `draft` stays null, the field stays transparent and the rolling overlay stays. The judge noted this but dismissed it. It is a reachable visible difference: the port shows plain text with the 4% focus tint and Escape becomes defaultPrevented, while the original shows neither. The checklist item typed-entry says typing opens a draft, so this is at most a small deviation.

defects: stamp-bump (differs from the ORIGINAL's real behaviour, although it matches the checklist and the source comment): in the original a badge that was already there at first render never bumps. Measured on Add to cart: original cart badge scale stays 1.00 on every frame (inline style 'transform: none' 25 ms after the click, also on rapid presses, on 9+ and after the bell was cleared), Vue starts at 1.33x (1.36 measured vs 1.022 rest baseline), dips to 0.93x at about 130 ms and settles. Same for the bell's first automatic 2 to 3, 3 to 4, 4 to 5: original flat at 1.00, Vue bumps from 1.35. Only once the bell badge has been cleared and re-mounted does the original bump (1 to 2 after refill: original first frame 1.379, Vue 1.355, same curve, min 0.948 at about 117 to 133 ms). So the port moves where the original snaps in the demo's default state. This is very likely a bug in the original (AnimatePresence initial={false} switches off 'initial' for motion children mounted later under a first-render child); a human should decide whether the port or the original is right before publishing.

attribute (not a checklist item): the Vue port puts tabindex="-1" on both badge spans (outer 'block' span and inner pill) of all three badges, 6 elements in total; the original has no tabindex anywhere in the demo. They sit inside aria-hidden="true" with pointer-events none and are not Tab stops, so there is no user-visible effect, but it is an extra attribute the original does not have.

defects: counts-and-badges: the folder count badges are missing completely. Original folder tabs contain a pill badge (text '(3)', '(2)', '(18)', '(0)', 18.4px high, spot background when selected, muted grey otherwise); the Vue port renders an empty unknown element <slidingtabcountbadge> instead (button children: 'span slidingtabcountbadge(empty)', count = null). Folder tabs are therefore narrower: To ship 85.2px vs 102.7px, On the way 111.8 vs 130.3, Delivered 100.4 vs 121.8, Returns 89.5 vs 108.0. Visible in shots/sliding-tabs-vue-00-initial.png vs sliding-tabs-web-00-initial.png. Cause in source: the template uses <SlidingTabCountBadge>, but that name is only an export alias ('export { CountBadge as SlidingTabCountBadge }'), not a binding the <script setup> template can resolve.

accessible-names-items: folder tab names lose their counts. Chrome accessibility tree, original: tab 'To ship ( 3 )', 'On the way ( 2 )', 'Delivered ( 18 )', 'Returns ( 0 )'; Vue: tab 'To ship', 'On the way', 'Delivered', 'Returns'. Same cause as above.

Console: Vue logs the warning '[Vue warn]: Failed to resolve component: SlidingTabCountBadge' on every render (35 warnings in the main run, 16 in the reduced-motion run, 5 per layout run). It is console.warn, not console.error, so consoleErrors stays 0, but it is the direct trace of the missing badge.

tab-order-and-focus-ring ('nothing decorative receives focus') and attributes: the port adds tabindex="-1" to every motion element (underline bar, segment pill, folder surface and its two corner spans, dock pill, dock label, chip fill, check svg, panel content div); the original has no tabindex on any of them. Result: a mouse click lands focus on a decorative, partly aria-hidden node instead of the button. Measured document.activeElement after a click: dock Home -> 'span.relative.overflow-hidden "Home"' (original: button[radio] Home); chip Free shipping clicked on its left padding -> 'span.absolute.inset-0.rounded-full' (original: the button); segment Month and Week clicked on the padding -> 'span.absolute.inset-0.rounded-[5px]' (original: the radio button). Arrow keys and Space still worked afterwards because the events bubble, and the Tab sequence itself is unchanged.

missedDefects: No new defect found that the judge did not report. One accepted deviation deserves more weight. The dock highlight pill never stretches in the Svelte port, because the source only interpolates translate and marginRight from the old rect to the new one. The judge's own data shows the original pill peaking at 114.0px on Saved>Search before settling at 100.4px, while the Svelte pill grows monotonically 94.4->100.2px. On leftward moves its left edge trails by about 10px (x at 86ms: 64.2 original vs 74.5 Svelte; t90 83ms vs 116ms). The judge reported this and accepted it as within tolerance. The checklist only requires the indicator to slide and match the new item width, so it does not break the pass.

Source comparison of the Svelte port against the original found no other differences: role, aria-selected, aria-checked, aria-pressed, aria-controls, roving tabindex, arrow/Home/End handling, the 99+ cap and sr-only parentheses, folder flares, the chips check mark and the dock sr-only label all match. There is no tabindex on decorative spans, so the Vue focus-landing defect does not apply.

Visible in shots/checkout-steps-svelte-mid-back32-a.png: '4' sits at the card edge with a detached piece of ink line under it.

Cause, from the source: flip() in CheckoutSteps.svelte animates both width [before, after] (a real reflow that already moves the following siblings) and x [dx, 0] with the full dx, so the displacement is counted twice. Position settle is also later: 397 to 400ms against 347 to 349ms (about 15 percent, inside tolerance on its own).

defects: label-float: every label animation after the first one starts by moving the wrong way. On blur with an empty value the label first jumps up and shrinks before settling: y 9.2 to 5.7 (3.5 px above the floated position) and scale 0.865 to 0.807 at about 83 ms, then travels to 17.8, settling at about 333 ms. On the second and third focus the label first dips below its rest position: y peaks at 21.34 (rest is 17.8) and scale at 1.06 before floating, settling at 366 ms against 267 ms. Reproduced on ZIP (5 recordings) and Email (blur after clearing: min y 5.67, scale 0.80) in two separate runs. Only the very first focus after load matches the original. Raw frames: floating-field-raw-svelte-B-zip-blur-empty.json, -B-zip-focus-2.json, -B-zip-blur-empty-3.json.

strength-motion: the same wrong-way start affects the strength segments. On delete each fill first grows to scaleX 1.6 (hidden by the track's overflow) and only drops below full after about 165 ms, so the visible emptying starts about 130 ms late and each segment needs about 417 ms instead of about 333 ms (+25 percent): seg4 moves at 18 ms, is still at 1.12 at 167 ms, ends at 435 ms (original: starts shrinking at 50 ms, ends 383 ms); seg1 ends at 551 ms (original 500). A segment that has been filled and emptied before also fills slower on the next paste (seg1 433 ms against 350 ms). Order (4 first on delete, 1 first on paste) and the roughly 40 ms stagger are correct. Raw frames: floating-field-raw-svelte-D-pw-delete.json. defects: ended-state (minor, the only failing item): on first load the discount of the already-ended banner 4 ('25% OFF') fades from opacity 1 to 0.4 over about 150 ms, where the original shows 0.4 from the first painted frame. Measured in 4 of 4 loads (A, A reduced, B, B reduced). Vue early frames after navigation: t=145ms 1, 168ms 0.98, 184ms 0.895, 201ms 0.726, 217ms 0.583, 251ms 0.448, 301ms 0.4. defects: cta-press: the press spring starts with a stale velocity, so the scale first moves the wrong way. On release the original goes 0.97 > 0.9703 > 0.9732 > ... > 1.0008 > 1 (min 0.97, settled 157 ms); Svelte goes 0.97 > 0.9656 > 0.9582 > 0.9587 > 0.9635 > ... > 1.0009 > 1 (min 0.958, settled 175 to 178 ms). On every press after the first, and on Enter-key press, the original goes 1 > 0.9993 > 0.9958 > ... > 0.97 (max 1.000, reaches 0.97 at about 210 ms); Svelte goes 1 > 1.0106 > 1.0119 > 1.0082 > 1.0018 > 0.9948 > ... > 0.97 (max 1.012, reaches 0.97 at about 237 ms). The wrong-way excursion is 0.012 on a total travel of 0.03 (40 percent of the amplitude), reproduced in 3 of 3 releases and 2 of 2 repeat presses plus a separate probe run. Only the very first mouse press matches the original. Cause: tapScale calls ctl.stop() and then animate(node, { scale }, spring), which inherits the previous animation's velocity. Fix idea: start each press and release with velocity 0 (or drive one motion value).

missedDefects: Extra tabindex attribute on three elements. LowStockIndicator.vue sets `tabindex: -1` on the digit motion.span in Count, sets `tabindex: -1` on the sold-out marker motion.span in Result (next to `aria-hidden: "true"`), and sets tabindex="-1" on the bar-fill motion.span. The original low-stock-indicator.tsx has no tabindex anywhere. The judge's own snapshot records it: results.json vue steps.initial and steps.finalSnap give tabindexEls = ['span[tabindex=-1]'] on every card, versus [] for react. A tabindex=-1 element takes focus on mouse click, so clicking the visible digit can put focus on a span inside the status line, which the original cannot do. The judge saw the attribute and dismissed it with an unmeasured claim about click focus. It is a real attribute difference on a block whose checklist item is 'Focus never lands on any part of any indicator'.

defects: bar-mode: the bar spring is only correct for the first animated change. Every later change starts with a wrong initial velocity: the fill first moves the wrong way or shoots past the target, and timing is off by 40 to 90 percent. Measured over 10 consecutive changes (capacity 40, 1.4 s apart), fill ratio per frame: 0.5>0.25 first rises to 0.647; 0.25>0.5 first dips to 0.10; 1>0.5 first grows to 1.30 (bar 30% wider than its track); 1>0.05 peaks at 1.42; tHalf 188-212 ms and t95 354-387 ms versus the original's 136-141 ms and 319-324 ms with max/min never leaving the start-end range; 0.5>1 was instead too fast (tHalf 43-58 ms, t95 175 ms). Still wrong with 4 s between changes: 0.75>1 peaked at 1.39 and 1>0.5 went 1.00, 1.09, 1.12, 1.10, 1.06 before falling (original and Vue: monotonic 1.00, 0.998, 0.977, 0.938). Visible in shots/low-stock-indicator-svelte-01-barprobe-60-20-mid.png: 90 ms into 60>20 the fill sticks out past the right end of the track, while the original (react-01-barprobe-60-20-mid.png) is already at about 73%. Likely cause: barFill() calls motion animate(node, {scaleX}) again on the same element after stop(), which reuses a stale velocity.

defects: switch-keyboard / focus-ring (switch): a mouse click on the switch does not focus the button, it focuses an inner decorative span. The port puts tabindex="-1" on 8 motion spans inside the switch (track-night, key, press, key-day, key-night, 3 rings), which makes them click-focusable. Measured: click on the track at (x+100, y+4) -> document.activeElement = SPAN tabindex=-1 class "absolute inset-0" (original and Svelte: BUTTON role=switch). Pressing Space/Enter afterwards still toggles, but the switch never matches :focus-visible (swFV=false, box-shadow none), so the designed 2px ring + 2px offset never appears; the original shows it (swFV=true, ring box-shadow present). Visible in shots/theme-picker-{orig,vue,svelte}-f1-trackclick-then-keys.png (montage tp-m-f1-trackclick-then-keys.png): original and Svelte show the ring around the switch, Vue shows none. Same after every mouse click in the main run (swClick end: act=span in Vue, act=button[switch] in original). Fix: do not put tabindex on the track span; if the motion-v press span needs it, keep focus on the button.
